learningObjective: Reason about the KV cache dataflow during a single autoregressive decode step and its interaction with attention kernels.

canonicalClaims.claim: One decode step writes one K and one V entry per sequence (size H_kv*d each) and reads the entire KV cache of the sequence (size seq_len * H_kv * d) to compute attention. Reads dominate for typical seq_len.
conditions: MHA/MQA/GQA structure with H_kv KV heads.
nonImplications: Does not imply paged vs contiguous storage changes total bytes read.

canonicalClaims.claim: In MQA/GQA, the same K/V is used by multiple Q heads; efficient attention kernels stage K/V once in SMEM per token and reuse across query heads, avoiding redundant HBM reads.
conditions: Kernel is designed with per-token or per-tile K/V staging.
nonImplications: Does not imply the reuse eliminates all KV read; only redundant reads across Q heads within a token.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention is strictly slower per attention step than a contiguous KV layout because of pointer indirection.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Paging adds a small indirection cost but avoids fragmentation costs; per-step latency is comparable in practice.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization has no effect on decode latency.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Decode is bandwidth-bound on KV; fewer bytes = lower latency.

misconceptions.claim: Decode is compute-bound on the attention softmax.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Attention flops scale with seq_len while KV reads also scale linearly; the memory ratio makes it bandwidth-bound.

implementationFacts: vLLM PagedAttention stores KV in fixed-size blocks (e.g., 16 tokens) referenced by block tables.
GQA/MQA cut per-token KV bandwidth by H/H_kv factor.
performanceScenarios: Long-context decode is essentially KV-read-bound; batch size is limited by KV cache capacity.
